# Introduction {#sec-intro}

Language models routinely act on information they have not written down. A model
completing a rhyming couplet selects its rhyme before it writes the line that ends
in it [@lindsey2025biology; @hanna2026latent]. A model asked for the result of a
calculation, or to make a choice and reveal it later, must hold or reconstruct that
content across the tokens it writes in between. How such unwritten information
reaches the position that uses it is a basic question about autoregressive
computation. It is also a practical one. Chain-of-thought monitoring assumes that
the reasoning relevant to a decision passes through, or can be recovered from, the
text the model writes [@korbak2025monitorability; @baker2025monitoring]. The
central risk to that assumption is content that travels in the model's state while
the text says nothing about it [@pfau2024dots; @roger2023steganography;
@turpin2023unfaithful; @chen2025reasoning].

In a transformer, information present at one position can reach a later position
by three paths (@fig-overview A). It can be **emitted**: it changes the tokens the
model writes, which are then read back as input. It can be **retrieved directly**:
the later position attends to the position where the information originates, or
to the visible text from which it can be recomputed. Or it can be **relayed**:
intermediate positions, including the model's own generated tokens, pick it up and
pass it forward. Only relay keeps content in the model's state while the
intervening text is silent about it, so relay is what a text monitor could miss.
Prior work establishes that planning signals exist and are causally used: they are
decodable ahead of time [@pal2023futurelens; @wu2024plan; @men2024lookahead],
visible in attribution graphs [@lindsey2025biology; @hanna2026latent], and steerable
at the planning site [@maar2026plan; @ma2026plan; @jacopin2026improvisation]. These
methods locate where a plan is formed or can be changed. They do not measure which
path the plan takes to the position where it is used.

We introduce **route accounting**, a decomposition of an intervention's effect by
path (@sec-method). A donor's hidden states are written at the source positions, and
the effect is measured where the information is used. Clamping the states of chosen
groups of positions to their clean or edited values, at every layer, isolates each
path. Emission is separated from persistence by fixing the generated text. Within
persistence, direct retrieval is separated from relay, with sufficiency and
necessity versions for every group of intermediate positions and an explicit
interaction term. Because a method that never finds relay would be uninformative, we
validate route accounting on induction [@olsson2022induction], where relay through
the copied token's position is the known mechanism. In that positive control, the
accounting assigns the effect to relay, while direct retrieval stays at or below 3%
of the effect in six of seven models (@fig-overview B).

Applied to four tasks in 15 checkpoints from three model families, route accounting
reveals a consistent principle: **look it up, don't carry it**. Unwritten information
is read, near the point of use, from a fixed position in the prompt. That position is
either the source itself or a copy stored at a structural token next to it. The
information is not carried along the generated text (@tbl-map). Rhyme plans reach
the rhyme mainly by direct retrieval of the rhyme word: 68 to 95% of persistence in
all but one configuration (@sec-lookup). Values computed from the prompt are
recomputed from their visible sources at the answer, even where this fails. No
downstream position holds the running value of a variable chain, even as a block.
When intermediate values are written out, the answer follows them: emission carries
83 to 99% of the effect (@sec-emission). Relay along generated text more than three
positions before the target never exceeds 1% of persistence in couplets. For computed
values and hidden choices, relay through all intermediate positions is at most 2.4%
of the effect, and in most models its interval includes zero.

A regularity found under favourable conditions is only as strong as the tests that
could have broken it. We therefore test the principle in three settings designed to
make carrying necessary or undetectable, each with a decision rule fixed before the
result (@sec-stress):

- **Recurrent memory.** In a hybrid where three of every four layers pass information
  forward only through a recurrent state [@yang2025gateddeltanet], relay is the only
  path available to most of the network. The recurrent memory nevertheless carries
  2 to 4% of the plan at 4B, 9B and 27B parameters.
- **Distance.** Gemma 3 interleaves five local attention layers with a 1,024-token
  window per global layer [@gemma3]. Beyond that window, most layers cannot read the
  source. At 2,000 tokens, the 27B model reads a stored copy at the line's final
  token, which is necessary for about half of the effect. Relay along the generated
  line rises only to about 12%, the largest value we observe. A 12B model, which
  stores no such copy, loses the plan instead of relaying it.
- **Hidden content.** A choice that a reader cannot infer from the text is the case
  monitoring cares about most. Models store part of a secret pick at a predictable,
  low-content token of the instruction. In Gemma 3 27B, most of the stored pick sits
  on the word *the* in "about the weather". The pick is read directly at the reveal.
  At most 2% of it is relayed through the intervening sentence, and none of it is
  written into the sentence.

Across scale, the one route that grows is storage at the line's final token: the
comma in chat prompts, the newline in plain prompts (@sec-storage). It appears from
14B in Qwen3 and at 12 to 27B in Gemma 3, and is present in base checkpoints, so it is
learned in pretraining. This result reconciles published accounts of where the rhyme
plan lives. The account that the plan is read from the rhyme word
[@hanna2026latent] and the account that it is placed at the line boundary
[@lindsey2025biology; @ma2026plan] describe two lookup sites that coexist. Their
proportions depend on scale, family and prompt format.

**Contributions.**

1. Route accounting: a path-level decomposition of intervention effects in
   autoregressive generation. It separates emission from persistence, and direct
   retrieval from relay, and reports sufficiency, necessity and interaction for
   every group of positions. It is validated on a positive control.
2. A principle with its evidence: unwritten information is looked up, not carried.
   The evidence covers visible plans, computed values and hidden choices, across
   families, sizes, prompt formats and instruct versus base checkpoints. It holds
   under the authors' published feature steering as well as under state edits.
3. Three pre-registered stress tests (recurrent memory, attention distance, hidden
   content) that bound where the principle holds and quantify the largest deviation
   we observe.
4. A scale law for storage at the line's final token, and a reconciliation of the
   published accounts of rhyme planning.

Where unwritten information travels. Each cell gives the share of the effect
carried by a path, as a range over the models tested, from the largest effect
measured in each setting. Route: *emission*, the effect through the text the model
writes; *retrieval or storage*, a later position reads the source, a stored copy of
it, or the visible sources from which it recomputes the content; *relay*, the effect
carried along intermediate positions. Observability: *visible* content can be
recovered by a reader of the text; *hidden* content cannot. Dashes mark cells that
the design rules out. Sections and figures give the full results with 95% intervals.

:::
